categories.name: Isaiah
categories.description: Prophecies of judgment, hope, and the coming Messiah

categories.name: Jeremiah
categories.description: The weeping prophet's warnings to Judah

categories.name: Ezekiel
categories.description: Visions of judgment, exile, and restoration

categories.name: Daniel
categories.description: Faithfulness in exile and visions of the future

quizQuestions.prompt: What sign did Isaiah prophesy about a virgin bearing a son, later understood as pointing to Jesus?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

options.text: A virgin shall conceive and bear a son called Immanuel
A star shall appear over Bethlehem
A new temple shall be built in a day
A king shall rise from Egypt

quizQuestions.prompt: What names does Isaiah 9:6 give to the child who would be born, called "Wonderful, Counsellor"?
quizQuestions.explanation: "His name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace."

options.text: Wonderful, Counsellor, Mighty God, Prince of Peace

quizQuestions.prompt: What vision did Isaiah receive in the Temple that called him into prophetic ministry?
quizQuestions.explanation: Isaiah saw the Lord high and lifted up, with seraphim calling "Holy, holy, holy."

options.text: He saw the Lord high and lifted up, with seraphim crying "Holy, holy, holy"
He saw a valley of dry bones
He saw a wheel within a wheel
He saw four beasts and a throne

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Isaiah say when God asked, "Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?"
quizQuestions.explanation: Isaiah responded, "Here am I; send me."

quizQuestions.prompt: What famous chapter in Isaiah describes a suffering servant "wounded for our transgressions"?
quizQuestions.explanation: Isaiah 53 prophetically describes a suffering servant, understood by Christians as pointing to Jesus' sacrifice.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Isaiah 40:31 promise to those who wait upon the LORD?
quizQuestions.explanation: "They that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles."

options.text: They shall renew their strength like eagles
They shall live forever on earth

quizQuestions.prompt: What weapons does Isaiah 2:4 say nations will beat into farming tools, a picture of future peace?
quizQuestions.explanation: "They shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks."

quizQuestions.prompt: What Persian king does Isaiah name in prophecy, over a century before he was born, as God's instrument to free the exiles?
quizQuestions.explanation: Isaiah names Cyrus by name as God's "shepherd" and "anointed" who would let the exiles return.

quizQuestions.prompt: What voice does Isaiah 40:3 say cries out in the wilderness, later applied to John the Baptist?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD."

options.text: "Prepare ye the way of the LORD"
"The kingdom of heaven is at hand"

quizQuestions.prompt: What object did a seraphim touch to Isaiah's mouth to symbolically purge his sin?
quizQuestions.explanation: A live coal from the altar was touched to his lips.

options.text: A live coal from the altar

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Isaiah 53, how is the suffering servant described in relation to sheep?
quizQuestions.explanation: "All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way."

options.text: "All we like sheep have gone astray"
"He shall feed his flock like a shepherd" only
"The lamb shall lie down with the wolf"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Isaiah 11 prophesy will happen between a wolf and a lamb in the future kingdom of peace?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb" — a picture of restored peace in creation.

options.text: The wolf shall dwell with the lamb
The wolf shall be tamed as a pet
The lamb shall be given great strength
They shall both be removed from earth

quizQuestions.prompt: What comfort does Isaiah 40 open with, repeating the word twice?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God."

options.text: "Fear not, for I am with thee"

quizQuestions.prompt: In Isaiah's vision, what did the seraphim have that they used to fly and to cover their faces and feet?
quizQuestions.explanation: The seraphim each had six wings.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Isaiah 1:18 say Israel's sins, though as scarlet, shall become?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow."

quizQuestions.prompt: Which two kingdoms threatened Judah, prompting King Ahaz's fear that led to the Immanuel prophecy?
quizQuestions.explanation: Syria (Aram) and the northern kingdom of Israel allied against Judah, causing Ahaz to fear.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Isaiah walk around doing for three years as a prophetic sign against Egypt and Ethiopia?
quizQuestions.explanation: Isaiah walked barefoot and without his outer garment as a sign of coming captivity.

options.text: Walked barefoot and without his outer robe
Carried a yoke on his shoulders

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Isaiah 53:7, how did the suffering servant respond when afflicted, compared to an animal?
quizQuestions.explanation: "He is brought as a lamb to the slaughter... he openeth not his mouth."

options.text: Silent, like a lamb led to slaughter
Fought back fiercely, like a lion

quizQuestions.prompt: What did God tell Jeremiah about knowing him even before he was born?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee... I ordained thee a prophet."

options.text: "Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee"
"I will make thee a great nation"
"I have chosen thy father before thee"

quizQuestions.prompt: What excuse did Jeremiah first give God for not wanting to be a prophet?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeremiah said, "I cannot speak: for I am a child."

quizQuestions.prompt: What container did Jeremiah watch a potter reshape, illustrating God's power over nations?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeremiah watched a potter remake a marred vessel of clay into a new one.

options.text: A clay vessel on a potter's wheel

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jeremiah wear on his neck as a prophetic sign that Judah should submit to Babylon's rule?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeremiah wore a wooden yoke as a symbol of coming submission to Babylon.

quizQuestions.prompt: What promise does Jeremiah 29:11 give about God's thoughts toward His people?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I know the thoughts that I think toward you... thoughts of peace, and not of evil."

options.text: Thoughts of peace, to give an expected end

quizQuestions.prompt: Who was Jeremiah's scribe, who wrote down his prophecies on a scroll?
quizQuestions.explanation: Baruch served as Jeremiah's faithful scribe.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did King Jehoiakim do to the scroll of Jeremiah's prophecies after hearing it read?
quizQuestions.explanation: The king cut the scroll with a knife and burned it in the fire.

options.text: Sent it to the priests for review

quizQuestions.prompt: Where was Jeremiah thrown for prophesying discouraging words to the army during the siege of Jerusalem?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeremiah was lowered into a muddy cistern (dungeon) and left to sink in the mire.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who rescued Jeremiah from the muddy cistern by pulling him out with ropes?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ebed-melech, an Ethiopian official, rescued Jeremiah with the king's permission.

quizQuestions.prompt: What new arrangement does Jeremiah 31 prophesy God will make with His people, written on their hearts?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeremiah prophesies a new covenant, with God's law written on the heart instead of stone.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which empire did Jeremiah repeatedly warn Judah would conquer them if they didn't repent?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeremiah warned that Babylon would conquer Judah as God's instrument of judgment.

quizQuestions.prompt: How long did Jeremiah prophesy Judah would serve the king of Babylon in exile?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeremiah prophesied seventy years of exile in Babylon.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jeremiah buy as a prophetic act of hope, even as Jerusalem was under siege?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeremiah bought a field at Anathoth, a sign that life and property would matter again after exile.

quizQuestions.prompt: Because of his difficult, sorrowful message, what nickname is Jeremiah often given?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeremiah is often called "the weeping prophet" for his deep sorrow over Judah's sin and coming judgment.

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Jeremiah 20, what happened when Jeremiah tried to stop speaking God's word out of frustration?
quizQuestions.explanation: He said God's word was like fire shut up in his bones, and he could not hold it in.

options.text: It was like fire in his bones, he could not hold it in
God released him from his calling

quizQuestions.prompt: What event is the book of Lamentations mourning throughout its five poems?
quizQuestions.explanation: Lamentations mourns the destruction of Jerusalem and the Temple by Babylon.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which prophet is traditionally credited with writing Lamentations?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jeremiah is traditionally credited as the author, matching his role as an eyewitness to Jerusalem's fall.

quizQuestions.prompt: What hopeful truth does Lamentations 3 declare in the middle of deep grief, about God's compassions?
quizQuestions.explanation: "His compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness."

options.text: His mercies are new every morning

quizQuestions.prompt: What literary structure do most chapters of Lamentations follow, tied to the Hebrew alphabet?
quizQuestions.explanation: Most chapters are acrostics, with verses beginning with successive letters of the Hebrew alphabet.

quizQuestions.prompt: How does the book describe the city of Jerusalem at its opening, once full of people?
quizQuestions.explanation: "How doth the city sit solitary, that was full of people!"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does the writer of Lamentations 3 say is good to do quietly while waiting for the Lord's salvation?
quizQuestions.explanation: "It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD."

quizQuestions.prompt: How does the book of Lamentations end, with what kind of request to God?
quizQuestions.explanation: It ends with a prayer asking God to turn His people back to Himself and renew their days.

options.text: A prayer for God to renew and restore them

quizQuestions.prompt: What extreme suffering during the siege of Jerusalem does Lamentations 4 describe mothers resorting to?
quizQuestions.explanation: The famine was so severe that some mothers resorted to eating their own children.

options.text: Eating their own children in famine

quizQuestions.prompt: What striking vision did Ezekiel see of dry bones coming back to life?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezekiel saw a valley of dry bones that came together, gained flesh, and were filled with the breath of life.

options.text: A valley of dry bones coming to life

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Ezekiel see in his opening vision, involving four living creatures and wheels?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezekiel saw a vision of God's glory with four living creatures and wheels within wheels.

options.text: Four living creatures and wheels within wheels

quizQuestions.prompt: What did God have Ezekiel eat as part of his prophetic calling?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezekiel was told to eat a scroll, which tasted as sweet as honey.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Ezekiel do for over a year as a prophetic sign of the coming siege of Jerusalem?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezekiel lay on his side for an extended period, symbolizing the years of Israel's and Judah's punishment.

options.text: Lay on his side for many days

quizQuestions.prompt: What title does God frequently call Ezekiel throughout the book?
quizQuestions.explanation: God repeatedly addresses Ezekiel as "son of man."

quizQuestions.prompt: What role does Ezekiel 33 say a prophet serves for the nation, warning of coming danger?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezekiel is appointed a watchman, responsible to warn the people of coming judgment.

quizQuestions.prompt: What promise does Ezekiel 36 make about God giving His people a new kind of heart?
quizQuestions.explanation: "A new heart also will I give you... I will take away the stony heart... and give you an heart of flesh."

options.text: A new heart of flesh, instead of stone
A heart free from all feeling

quizQuestions.prompt: Where was Ezekiel living and prophesying when he received most of his visions?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezekiel prophesied among the exiles in Babylon, by the river Chebar.

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to Ezekiel's wife, which he was told not to publicly mourn as a sign to Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezekiel's wife died suddenly, and he was instructed not to mourn openly, as a sign of the coming shock to Israel.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Ezekiel prophesy would happen to the dry bones once breath entered them?
quizQuestions.explanation: They became a great army, standing up alive.

options.text: They became a great living army

quizQuestions.prompt: What vision does Ezekiel end the book with, involving water flowing from a restored building?
quizQuestions.explanation: Ezekiel envisions a river flowing from a restored temple, bringing life wherever it goes.

options.text: A river flowing from a restored temple

quizQuestions.prompt: According to Ezekiel 18, what principle does God teach about who bears responsibility for sin?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The soul that sinneth, it shall die" — each person is responsible for their own sin, not their parents'.

options.text: Each person is responsible for their own sin
Children bear their parents' guilt forever

quizQuestions.prompt: What den did Daniel survive a night in unharmed, after being falsely accused?
quizQuestions.explanation: Daniel was thrown into a den of lions and emerged unharmed.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Daniel and his three friends refuse to eat at the Babylonian king's table?
quizQuestions.explanation: They refused the king's rich food and wine, choosing vegetables and water instead.

options.text: The king's rich food and wine

quizQuestions.prompt: What were the Babylonian names given to Daniel's three friends, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah?
quizQuestions.explanation: They were renamed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego after they were thrown into a fiery furnace for refusing to worship an idol?
quizQuestions.explanation: They walked unharmed in the fire, joined by a fourth figure "like the Son of God."

options.text: They walked unharmed in the fire
They were burned but survived injured
They escaped before being thrown in

quizQuestions.prompt: What troubling dream did Daniel interpret for King Nebuchadnezzar, one showing the rise and fall of great kingdoms?
quizQuestions.explanation: Daniel interpreted a dream of a great statue with a gold head, representing successive kingdoms.

options.text: A statue made of different metals
A tree that was cut down

quizQuestions.prompt: What decree did King Darius's officials trick him into signing, which led to Daniel's punishment?
quizQuestions.explanation: They tricked Darius into decreeing that no one could pray to any god or man except the king for 30 days.

options.text: Only the king could be prayed to for 30 days

quizQuestions.prompt: What mysterious handwriting appeared on the wall during King Belshazzar's feast?
quizQuestions.explanation: The words "Mene, Mene, Tekel, Upharsin" appeared, which Daniel interpreted as judgment on the kingdom.

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to King Belshazzar the very night the writing on the wall appeared?
quizQuestions.explanation: Belshazzar was killed that night, and his kingdom was taken by the Medes and Persians.

options.text: He was killed and his kingdom taken

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to King Nebuchadnezzar for seven years after boasting of his own greatness?
quizQuestions.explanation: He was driven from among men and lived like an animal, eating grass, until he acknowledged God's sovereignty.

options.text: He lived like an animal, eating grass
He was imprisoned by his own army
He lost his kingdom to Egypt

quizQuestions.prompt: How many times a day did Daniel continue to pray, even after the decree against it was signed?
quizQuestions.explanation: Daniel continued to pray three times a day, just as he always had.

quizQuestions.prompt: What vision did Daniel have of "one like the Son of man" coming with the clouds of heaven?
quizQuestions.explanation: Daniel saw a vision of one like the Son of man given dominion, glory, and an everlasting kingdom.

options.text: One given an everlasting kingdom and dominion

quizQuestions.prompt: What food and drink did Daniel and his friends prove could keep them healthy, in a ten-day test?
quizQuestions.explanation: They ate vegetables and drank water, and looked healthier than those who ate the king's rich food.
